ownership_reason: The callee StrMatcher.StringMatcher.isMatch returns the number of characters it matched (2 for the suffix "}}"): its @return says so, its body returns chars.length, and StrMatcherTest.testStringMatcher_String/testMatcherIndices assert 2 for a two-character matcher. The other callers of the same callee use that value as a length and are covered by passing tests with multi-character string matchers: StrBuilder.replaceImpl(StrMatcher,...) removes removeLen characters (StrBuilderTest.testReplace_StrMatcher_String_int_int_int_VaryMatcher with stringMatcher("cb")) and StrTokenizer.readWithQuotes skips ignoredLen characters (StrTokenizerTest.testBasicIgnoreTrimmed4 with stringMatcher("IGNORE")). StrBuilder.replace(int,int,String) removes exactly [startIndex, endIndex) (StrBuilderTest.testReplace_int_int_String), and StrSubstitutor.resolveVariable documents endPos as the end of the variable including the suffix. StrSubstitutor.substitute is the only method that turns the suffix match into endPos: after a suffix match it advances pos by one character (pos++) instead of by endMatchLen, unlike its own prefix handling (pos += startMatchLen), so for a two-character suffix endPos stops inside the suffix and one suffix character survives the replacement. With the default one-character suffix '}' both forms coincide, which is why only a multi-character suffix exposes it. Restoring pos += endMatchLen fixes the trigger and keeps every test passing; any one-line change to isMatch or StrBuilder.replace that hides the stray character breaks the passing tests above.
